recipes.title: Restart, start or stop a service

steps.say: On Hosts select the server the step names (the one you would ssh into) - Cockpit manages one machine at a time.
Open Services - the systemd units on that server and their state.
Press the {1} button - Cockpit runs the same systemctl command for you, as root.

recipes.verify: The unit's State changes; the action is recorded like the console command.

steps.say: Open Services and select {1}: its state, since when, and its recent log lines show why it fails.
Select the server, open Services and press Reload units - systemd re-reads the unit file you edited.
Open Logs - the systemd journal of that machine.
Filter to the service {1} and press Show; the error lines name what broke.
Select the server, open Logs and choose Everything - kernel messages such as the OOM killer are listed with the rest.
Open Storage - filesystems with how full they are, the largest directories, and deleted files still held open (space df counts but du cannot see).
Select the server, open Networking and read Listening ports - which process owns which port.
Select the server, open Networking and read Firewall - the rules that decide who may connect.
Select the server: Overview shows CPU, memory and load, and Metrics shows how they changed - a quick way to spot the busy machine.

recipes.title: Run the command in Cockpit's terminal

steps.say: Select the server the step names on Hosts.
Open Terminal - a shell on that server, exactly like ssh from the console.
Type the command and press Enter.

recipes.verify: The output appears below; the command is recorded like one typed after ssh.
